utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this statement under 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, there's also one associated exhibit which is 1D15014 that was not on our 65 ter list, as we had not interviewed this witness at the time that this was filed so we would ask that that be added and admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I've already identified my objections to paragraph 36 which I understood was going to be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, paragraph 36 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think I heard that in a serious sense. What's the line of your objection, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I can note the Trial Chamber asked us earlier to provide the Chamber with advance notice of [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I know there was something but I didn't have --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- time to read it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The objection was that the entire paragraph is simply in reference to a document which has not been translated and which we did not receive. So it no longer -- in that respect it's no longer apposite. So on that basis alone I made the objection. I might have gone on under other circumstances to note that it appears to be commentary about a document that has -- is not linked to -- in any way to the witness's personal knowledge and about which he could not offer elucidation from his own experience, but instead commented -- analysed the document. So for a number of reasons that would have been subject to redaction, but I understood from the Defence that in light of the translation issue they were prepared to agree with the objection and redact the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Since the document has to be led live in any event, then it's not necessary that the paragraph remain in there and the same information will be -- or can be elicited by Dr. Karadzic live.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But the issue remains whether this witness is an appropriate person to deal with this document and whether this is admissible after having heard the evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's correct. And my e-mail also noted that the length of the document was such that I considered that it would be so handicapped in not being able to grasp the totality of the evidence that was being discussed in part, that I thought it wasn't appropriate to -- an appropriate option to simply lead it live given the length. But I know the Chamber often wants to hear it, but I didn't want to acquiesce in that without noting what I had said in the e-mail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us see how it evolves, Mr. Tieger. Yes, we'll admit the Rule 92 ter statement as well as the associated exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Those will be Exhibits D3133 and Exhibit D3134 respectively, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will now read a short summary of Mr. Cvijetin Simic's statement and then I will present an exhibit that's already in evidence which is in accord with this associated exhibit and lead some of this live. I will read in English. [In English] Cvijetin Simic was born on 24th of January, 1958, in Bijeljina and currently resides in the village of Velika Obarska. He was the president of the Bijeljina Municipal Assembly. The SDS party was established following the formation of the SDA and the HDZ, when it became clear that organising politically was the only way for the Serbian people in BiH to protect their own interests. The HDZ and the SDA acted exclusively in the interests of the Croat and Muslims respectively and the latter in particular worked to incite interethnic intolerance in Bijeljina. In November 1990, the Bijeljina local authority was formed on the basis of the election results. Although the SDS clearly won these elections, a coalition was formed with the SDA to protect and improve interethnic relations in the municipality. During this period, groups of Muslims were crossing to Croatia to join paramilitary organisations and fight against the JNA units. In September 1991 the JNA mobilised in Bijeljina. The SDA leaders successfully encouraged the Muslim population to ignore call-ups, whereas the Serbian -- Serbs in Bijeljina responded. This explains the interethnic composition of the JNA at this time. Relations between Serbs and Muslims deteriorated significantly in this period. SDA authorities co-ordinated the illegal delivery of weapons from Croatia and the arming of the Muslim population. Illegal, armed groups of Muslims began to form in the municipality. The authorities of Bijeljina Municipal Assembly were against all illegal organisations. When a group of officers from the Bijeljina garrison secretly distributed weapons to civilians they were stopped, the weapons returned, and the instigators punished. When on 15th of October, 1991, the Muslim and Croat leadership in BH voted to withdraw from Yugoslavia, the SDS began to form Serbian autonomous districts. The aim of these districts was always to bring normalcy to the lives of the civilians where possible. The political differences between Muslims and Serbs and the extremely deteriorated ethnic relations led to open conflicts between the parties. The Bijeljina Municipal Assembly was committed to and sincere in maintaining peace in the municipality. When, for instance, a Serb threw a bomb on a Muslim cafe, senior Serb officials in Bijeljina Municipal Assembly carried out a thorough investigation of the incident and the perpetrator was imprisoned. In late March 1992, Muslim formations instigated a general blockade of Bijeljina and it was clear these activities had been planned in advance. By the 1st of April, street battles were -- had broken out throughout the town. Mr. Cvijetin Simic was barricaded and threatened and came to the conclusion that these activities were organised by SDA leaders. At a meeting to resolve the conflict that Cvijetin Simic attended, the SDA president refused to disarm the Muslim population and lift the barricades unless UN observers first came to the city. Mr. Cvijetin Simic concluded that the SDA leadership wished to continue the conflict as long as possible in order to accomplish their political and military aims. On April the 2nd, armed Muslims took control of the hospital and civilians were prevented from receiving medical care. The Muslim-controlled state media meanwhile put out false reports and propaganda alleging falsely that Serbs attacked Muslims in Bijeljina; there had been thousands of Muslim fatalities. Throughout this period the Bijeljina municipality assembly operated transparently. There was no need to form parallel institutions of authority, and hence the Crisis Staff did not adopt any decision and Cvijetin Simic was not a member of any Crisis Staff. Mr. Simic and his colleagues in Bijeljina municipality worked always with the aim of normalising life and work for all citizens. Paramilitary organisations were not tolerated. On the other hand, Muslim leaders such as Hasan Tiric organised attacks on the legitimate organs of authority in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I should now like to ask you -- you mentioned Mr. Tiric. Do you have firsthand knowledge of Mr. Tiric and his actions?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC
utterances.text: I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second -- yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let's try to keep the record straight. He actually didn't mention Mr. Tiric, that's in the redacted portion of the statement. But ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now I see the point. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I still don't understand why this would be redacted. This is already in evidence and we have displayed it before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You agreed to redact it, but here already -- no, could you reformulate your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, it was your impression that what happened on the evening of the 1st -- 31st of March was well-organised and synchronised. Could you tell us by whom and who was the most prominent leader of those units that took over the town?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC
utterances.text: During those days, as I described in my statement, I passed several of those roadblocks set up by armed Muslim persons. It was quite obvious. We later even asked for a meeting of the National Defence Council in Bijeljina, I mentioned that in my statement, on the 1st of April. Out of the Muslim representatives, there was the president of the SDA, the TO staff commander, and I believe one deputy to the Municipal Assembly of Bijeljina, a Muslim. And from those meetings and from the times I passed through the town, I was able to conclude that these roadblocks and this take-over was organised by the SDA, the Party of Democratic Action. At that time I did not know yet who the main organisers were, and that's why I tried with the president of the party, whose name was Zenaid, I believe, to solve these problems. However, a few days later in the Croatian media there appeared reports that were taken over by our media where Mr. Tiric is named as the leader and he was calling upon those who had left, his fighting men, to come back and take Bijeljina back. That was reported by the Croatian media and those reports were reprinted by our own media and all over Yugoslavia. In 1993 and 1994 and also in 1992 there was an investigation concerning this armed insurgency and these problems in the town. And 60 to 70 witness statements were collected during the investigation that I didn't see at the time, but I found out later. And these statements helped shed light on who organised this insurgency in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see D01608, please, in e-court. There's also a translation. This is a document that's been admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at this first paragraph. Which formation is involved and who is mentioned as being the commander? First of all, let me introduce this document. This is a document of the Ministry of Defence of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. The date is the 9th of May, 1996, and they are providing information about Crni Labudovi, the Black Swans. What do you know about the Black Swans?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't know much. I know that it was a special unit, I think, in Zivinice in the Federation of BH.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then in the first paragraph --

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC
utterances.text: I see here that their intention is to take Bijeljina. We did not know then that that is what they were called.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I see. So the official date of the establishment of the unit is the 31st of March, 1992. On that day, acting on orders from Vahid Karavelic and the mentioned Captain Swan, Hasan Tiric, the present commander of the Black Swans unit and about 15 members of the Patriotic League found themselves in Bijeljina with the task of forming a special purposes unit, and at that time he allegedly was to oppose the VRS forces in their attempt to take Bijeljina. How does this tally with what you know about the beginning of the conflict in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just before you answer. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, everything we've heard from the witness so far is that he wasn't aware of this type of information at the time. He's been candid with us about that, to his credit. Why Dr. Karadzic now chooses to trot out this document and run a kind of history channel educational effort with this witness is beyond me and is not a productive use of his time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, the witness said that he didn't know that that is what they were called. I'm interested in what the witness knows, how this fits into his knowledge as to how and who started the conflict in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Just a second. Since the -- from previous page, lines 24, to page 96, line 20, the witness said some words which seems to be related to this. On that basis we'll allow the witness to answer the question. Yes, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this statement that I gave, I presented my view and my knowledge as to what was happening on the ground in town itself. And in view of the attempts to find a solution on the 1st and 2nd of April, I said that according to the information that we had and the information that was broadcast in the media afterwards, Hasan Tiric appeared as the leader of this rebellion in Bijeljina as the organiser. But I did not know, as I've said here, that the name of this unit was -- what was it? The Black Swans. I think that as far as what basically happened on the ground is concerned, it corresponds to what is written here. I mean, if I'm saying it corresponds to that, let me add something. On the 31st of -- on the evening of the 31st, these activities related to an armed rebellion started. This sentence is incorrect, oppose the Army of Republika Srpska, attempt to take Bijeljina. The VRS had no intention to take Bijeljina and I don't see why they would do it and from whom they would take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Army of Republika Srpska, did it exist on the 31st of March?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC
utterances.text: No. At that time there were units of the JNA in Bijeljina. The Army of Republika Srpska was established sometime at the end of May, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Bearing in mind your experience and this report of the Croatian intelligence service, do you have any doubts as to who it was who started the war and who came first, Arkan or Tiric?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. You can ask the witness if he knows but not based upon this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you confirm, or rather, how does this document fit into your own knowledge about the essence of what happened there? I asked you about that and you confirmed.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've already said that as far as events are concerned, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have any doubt as to who it was that started the war in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm going to object again. This is a fact witness and Dr. Karadzic is trying to transform him into somebody from he's seeking not-helpful opinions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please move on to your next topic, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions at this point in time for Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Simic, your evidence in chief in this case has been admitted in writing in lieu of your oral testimony. And now you will be cross-examined by the Prosecutor, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, let me begin with paragraph 12 of your statement, which mentions the October 15th session of the joint Assembly in Bosnia and Herzegovina, which as you indicated adopted the enactment confirming the sovereignty of the republic of BH. And then you said in your paragraph: "After this the SDS started forming Serbian autonomous districts in response to the activities of the SDA and HDZ in BH." Mr. Simic, did -- were you aware of a large plenary session on the 7th of September, 1991, at which decisions were taken on the next steps regarding regionalisation? As one person put it: "We'll split into Serbian Bosnia, Croat Bosnia, Muslim Bosnia ..." Were you aware of that meeting in early September 1991 about regionalisation? And that's a meeting of the SDS, sir.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't know now. I cannot remember exactly right now. There were meetings, several meetings. I don't know the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For benefit of the Court and the Defence, those references can be found at P2530, 2544, and 2545.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Simic, you may not recall that particular meeting, but did you miss the fact that in September of 1991 numerous SAOs were declared, that is, a month before what you told the Court in paragraph 12 was the trigger for the establishment of those bodies? And I'm referring specifically, for example, to SAO Herzegovina on the 12th of September, 1991; the Autonomous Region of Krajina on 16 September 1991; SAO north-Eastern Bosnia on 19 September 1991. Those events took place a month before or the month before what you claim to this Trial Chamber was the trigger for their formation.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC
utterances.text: I have documents, I don't know which documents the OTP has, but on the 28th of October, 1991, the Assembly of the region of North-East Bosnia was established. I think that it was perhaps on the 25th of October that the Municipal Assembly of Bijeljina reached a decision to accede to this agreement on regional organisation. On the basis of that decision of the Municipal Assembly of Bijeljina, I signed this agreement on the establishment of this autonomous region of North-East Bosnia and I think that this was on the 28th of October. As for these other regions, I did not take part in that and I wasn't really in charge of that -- well, now I may try to remember when it happened. But that wouldn't really matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So your position then, Mr. Simic, is that you're aware of or claim to be aware of the one -- of a regional formation that you were involved with, but accept that there was -- that the formation or establishment of SAOs elsewhere took place prior to that, correct, if that's what the evidence in this court shows?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, you said to me whether my information was correct, my statement, that on the 28th this region of North-East Bosnia was established. If that is correct, I think that the question -- well, I mean, I have documents and I can present them to you that that is when it was established. If you have something saying that it was established before that, let me see it. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah, we're going to take a look at that, but I'm going to move on for a moment in the interest of time, but we will return to that, the establishment of those municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And, by the way, for benefit of the Court those references can be found at P2536, pages 81 through 82.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, do you -- with respect to the establishment of those formations, you were aware that the purpose of the establishment of SAOs was considered by many members or by certain members of the SDS to destroy a unitary Bosnia and Herzegovina; correct? And that is what Bosnian Serb officials said in official forums at the time?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC
utterances.text: I can take part in a discussion on the basis of the documents that we adopted and discussed at the Municipal Assembly of Bijeljina, and it clearly says there what the objective of the organisation is, what the competences are, what the work is in this planned region. I mean, who said what where, I cannot comment on all of that. As I said, in the decision to accede to the agreement on the establishment of the region of North-East Bosnia, all the tasks, all the objectives, are stated there and I believe that you have that document as well. The objective was not to break up Bosnia and Herzegovina in that part, perhaps some decentralisation in some of the work involved; that is not stated in the documents that you referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the documents that I referred to, just to name a couple, are D456 at page 68, referring to the creation of the SAOs and districts; and D456 at page 70. You did speak about the function in the SAOs and I wanted to ask you about a couple of documents in connection with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could call up 65 ter 24793.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, while we're doing that I would like to raise an issue, this is now the second time that this has occurred, and that is that Prosecution has notified us that during this one-hour cross-examination they've given us a list of 51 potential exhibits. And of course you know that that list, pursuant to your order, is only given to us when the cross-examination starts. There's no way that the Prosecution can use 51 documents in an hour, and so this kind of notice puts us at a big disadvantage to be trying to go through 51 documents during Mr. Tieger's cross-examination to guess which one he's going to use. And I think that that's not fair. So I would ask that you either order the Prosecution to give us notice 24 hours in advance of the cross-examination or that you require the Prosecutor to be more focused and give us notice of the documents he truly expects to use if they're going to be doing it at this late stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This did not need to be hashed out here. If Mr. Robinson wanted to address that, we can talk about that. Listed on that notice are documents I intended to simply refer to by way of information that the Court has received, and out of courtesy alert the Defence to it. If that doesn't help, and I can understand that Mr. Robinson may want to parse through that, we can do that in two different ways. But that can be adjusted as needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, we have on the screen right now is -- should be 24793.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is a document that is dated -- should be dated the 13th of April and then also the 21st of April, as you will see. It's a request for an urgent reply and implementation of the decision of the Executive Council of the Semberija and Majevica SAO. And does this accurately reflect, insofar as you are aware, because you did talk about the functioning of the SAOs, how this would work; that is, that the SAO being on the ground and more familiar with local needs, would essentially nominate somebody and then turn to the ministry for actual implementation and authorisation of the decision?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I'm actually not able to find this document in e-court. So we'd like to at least have a copy e-mailed to us so we can follow other than just on the screen. There may be other pages of the document that are of interest to us in our re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Reid is working on it. I think I indicated the nature of the problem before and how we do our best to surmount it, but it continues to be a continuing problem. I noted that at some point in the earlier examination we temporarily overcame that uploading problem. Currently it persists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was wondering whether the witness could read it at all. Do you remember the question? Can you answer the question, Mr. Simic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can read the document. However, could I just see the date below? I cannot see it now. Could you scroll down a bit. I can answer the question, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sometime 21st of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Simic, I'm not looking for a description of this particular event but only if the relationship between the SAO government and the ministry as reflected here is consistent with your understanding of how that worked?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC
utterances.text: I know what the relations were between the Municipal Assembly of Bijeljina and this community and the appropriate ministries and institutions, and I can explain that. The Municipal Assembly proposed certain people for certain positions, and they asked for the consent of the relevant ministries and the acceptance of this proposal in some way by the ministry. I think that in this part the situation is similar. Now, whether it was that way in the documents as well, I was not an official of the region so I cannot say anything for sure, but I think that the Assembly of the region did meet sometime around the 20th or the 21st of April, and probably this reply was sought on the basis of the decision of the regional Assembly. And I believe that you also have that in the materials.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender this document and turn to one more; that's 65 ter 24790.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we object. We've never seen this document and it's very difficult to read. We're looking at one page. I don't see how it could be admitted without having been disclosed to us, but perhaps tomorrow we could look at it and let you know. I think it would be better, actually, since we only have a few minutes left to not proceed with any more documents today. I don't think it's fair to make us look at documents at the same time as the witness that have never been disclosed to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, that is very interesting in light of the constant submission of documents of large length led live over our objection about the concern. So this is a one-page document that they can't cope with. I have no objection to continuing, but that should tell us something about the nature of the process they've been pursuing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll receive this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6207, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And it's -- the logic also applies to the other direction. It's only five minutes. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I called up 65 ter 24790. That's an even smaller document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, this is a conclusion of the Serbian autonomous district of Semberija and Majevica following its meeting of the 22nd of May, 1992, and it refers to the decision of the Serbian Republic of BH on general mobilisation and concludes that it shall be implemented and directs that the district secretary for defence and the municipal secretary for defence shall be tasked with implementing that decision. So this is a reflection of that same relationship in the other direction; right, Mr. Simic? In the previous document we saw, the SAO turning to the ministry for implementation of some selections it had made, and here we see the SAO implementing the decisions of the Serbian republic; correct?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC
utterances.text: A decision cannot be carried out by way of a conclusion. This has to do with mobilisation, if I can read it, and this was done by municipal secretariats of national defence. Now, I don't know how the region could be carrying out mobilisation. What is written here is the municipal secretariat of national defence. They were the ones in charge of that, not the region. So that would be the conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Are you looking at the document, Mr. Simic? It says -- it's not so unclear. There's a decision -- let's take it step by step. The Serbian republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina made -- that is, the republic level made a decision on general mobilisation. The SAO indicates that it shall be implemented and then turns to the municipal secretariats for that purpose; correct?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN SIMIC
utterances.text: Over here they're asking for the decision to be implemented. At the same time they charge the secretariats for national defence to carry the decision out. Now, I don't know the exact competences, who issues an order for mobilisation. I think it's military units, the military. I don't know to what extent the civilian authorities are in charge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender that, Mr. President, and it looks like we're out of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'll object because I don't believe the witness has been able to comment on or confirm anything about the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: They're asking for the decision to be implemented at the same time they charge the secretariats for national defence to carry the decision out. What could be more clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Anybody can read a document, but if the witness confirms something in the document, then that should be the basis for admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If he's not confirming it, then I'm impeaching him. He's the one who raised the functioning of the SAOs in his statement, Mr. President, so one way or another it should go in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The rest of the day will calm down at bit further. We'll resume tomorrow at 9.00. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 20th day of March, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.
